title: Chapter 11 summary and quiz
recap: A generic API can combine deduced type parameters with explicit compile-time policy values. Keep the mathematical contract independent of the syntax used at the call site.
Exercise several specializations and boundary policies rather than a single happy-path instance. This catches accidentally fixed result types and hard-coded template values.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement clampValue<T>(value, low, high) and discounted<Percent,T>(price). clampValue returns low below the lower bound, high above the upper bound, or value inside; low <= high is guaranteed. discounted returns price*(100-Percent)/100.0 as double, preserving fractions. Percent is a compile-time integer in [0,100]; prices are finite and nonnegative. Both templates must work with int and double inputs.
hints: Write the clamp as three possible return paths.
Percent belongs in the template parameter list.
Use floating-point arithmetic before division in discounted.
